newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. unveils $440 mln welfare-to-work plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. unveils $440 mln welfare-to-work plan.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Monday unveiled a $440 million welfare-to-work program that includes $50 million to capitalize the state's infrastructure and economic development bank.

"There are few greater or more important challenges than helping our fellow Californians make a successful transition from welfare to work," Wilson, a Republican, said in a statement announcing his plan.

Wilson said his program would help create job opportunities for an estimated 600,000 people who will come off public assistance in the next three years under new federal and state welfare legislation.

The stakes are high for California. If the state fails to move at least a quarter of its caseload of welfare recipients into jobs by the end of 1997, the state could lose more than $187 million in federal block grant funding, the Wilson administration warned.
"Our economy has soared back," Wilson said. "There is plenty of work to be had."
* $277 million to expand child care services in California. This funding will provide services for nearly 120,000 additional children.

* $18.1 million to fund a job-match program using Internet technology. County welfare departments would receive $14.5 million to purchase, install and maintain 1,500 computers for welfare recipients to directly access job listings.
* $95 million for job training, education and economic development programs

* $50 million to capitalize the California Infrastructure and Economic Development Bank. The bank encourages private and public investment in infrastructure by issuing bonds and arranging private bond insurance. In January, Wilson proposed a $200 million bond measure to capitalize the bank.
* Reducing the state bank and corporations tax by 10 percent over two years.
